statement: If a number be the least that is measured by prime numbers, it will not be measured by any other prime number except those originally measuring it.
heath_proof: For let the number A be the least that is measured by the prime numbers B, C, D; I say that A will not be measured by any other prime number except B, C, D. For, if possible, let it be measured by the prime number E, and let E not be the same with any one of the numbers B, C, D. Now, since E measures A, let it measure it according to F; therefore E by multiplying F has made A. And A is measured by the prime numbers B, C, D. But, if two numbers by multiplying one another make some number, and any prime number measure the product, it will also measure one of the original numbers; [VII. 30] therefore B, C, D will measure one of the numbers E, F. Now they will not measure E; for E is prime and not the same with any one of the numbers B, C, D. Therefore they will measure F, which is less than A: which is impossible, for A is by hypothesis the least number measured by B, C, D. Therefore no prime number will measure A except B, C, D.
ai_proof_text:
9.14
**Statement:** If a number be the least that is measured by prime numbers, it will not be measured by any other prime number except those originally measuring it.

**Step 1.** Let A be the least number that is measured by the prime numbers B, C, D. Suppose, for the sake of contradiction, that A is also measured by some prime number E which is different from each of B, C, D.

**Step 2.** Since E measures A, by the definition of measurement there exists a number F such that A equals E multiplied by F [D7.15].

**Step 3.** Now B is prime and B measures A, that is, B measures the product of E and F. By 7.30, since a prime measuring a product must measure one of the factors, B measures E or B measures F.

**Step 4.** But E is prime, so by D7.11 it is measured by a unit alone. Since B is a prime number, B is not a unit [D7.1, D7.11]. And B is not equal to E, since E is different from each of B, C, D. Therefore B does not measure E.

**Step 5.** Consequently, from Step 3 and Step 4, B must measure F.

**Step 6.** By the same reasoning applied to C: since C is prime and measures the product E times F, by 7.30 either C measures E or C measures F. Since E is prime and C is a prime different from E, C does not measure E [D7.1, D7.11]. Therefore C measures F.

**Step 7.** Likewise for D: since D is prime and measures the product E times F, by 7.30 either D measures E or D measures F. Since E is prime and D is a prime different from E, D does not measure E [D7.1, D7.11]. Therefore D measures F.

**Step 8.** Therefore F is measured by each of B, C, D. But A is by hypothesis the least number measured by B, C, D. Hence A is less than or equal to F.

**Step 9.** However, since E is a prime number, E is at least 2, so E is greater than a unit. Therefore A, being E multiplied by F, is greater than F [CN5, D7.3]. That is, F is less than A.

**Step 10.** But Step 8 established that A is less than or equal to F, while Step 9 established that F is less than A. This is a contradiction.

**Step 11.** Therefore the supposition is false, and A is not measured by any prime number other than B, C, D. Q.E.D.
